No. If you don't repay an Instant Advance, Albert won't engage in debt collection activities, sell the amount to a third party, or report it to credit reporting agencies. There also isn't a legal or contractual claim against you for nonpayment.

Not repaying does have consequences, though. Your access to advances may be suspended, and the suspension can last 30 days or more (or 90 days or more) depending on how late the repayment is. Albert may also deny you future access to Instant Advance, and it reserves the right to set off the balance from your other Albert accounts.

One caveat: one help center article says late fees may apply, while the Terms of Use say there are no late fees on Instant Advances. If you're concerned about this, I'd suggest checking the details in the app or contacting support.
